newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Serb army detains own defence minister.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb army detains own defence minister.

text.p: Bosnian Serb Defence Minister Milan Ninkovic was held illegally at Bosnian Serb army headquarters on Tuesday, the interior ministry said, as top army commanders defied their sackings by civilian leaders.
Military police intercepted Ninkovic's car and he was keld for several hours, the ministry said.
Ninkovic, a deputy justice minister and two members of parliament were stopped in Han Pijesak, eastern Bosnia, and taken to the nearby bunker of General Ratko Mladic, the army's sacked commander.
Mladic and his general staff are resisting their dismissals, announced at the weekend by President Biljana Plavsic, and have refused to recognise General Pero Colic as the new commander.
The interior ministry did not say whether Mladic, who has been publicly supported by 100 high-ranking Bosnian Serb army officers, spoke to Ninkovic.
The dismissal of the army's wartime leadership was regarded as an attempt by the government to regain civilian political control over the army.
Colic claimed the support of Carl Bildt, the chief international mediator in Bosnia, who has been trying to secure Mladic's extradition for trial by a U.N. war crimes court in The Hague.
The new Serb commander met Bildt's military adviser, General Bertrand de la Presle, on Tuesday and told Bosnian Serb media that his appointment had been welcomed.

In a statement to Bosnia Serb radio, Colic said attacks by the Mladic camp on the new general staff were "a disgrace, especially the attacks of some superior officers who wish to create a rift in the Serb army".
He appealed to the dismissed generals to "show patriotism and help us as their co-fighters in creating a Serb army according to the will of the people".
